title: U.S. House · Indiana's 7th District

context.text: Incumbent André Carson won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 62.4% against three challengers. Patrick McAuley won the Republican primary with 84.4%. James Sceniak advanced from the Libertarian Party convention on March 22, 2026.

priorities.text: Supports initiatives to create jobs and stimulate the economy for families struggling with the cost of health care, food, and energy.
Supports expanding access to quality public education.
Supports a comprehensive energy strategy including wind, solar, nuclear, and biofuels alongside continued domestic production.

positions.summary: Supports continued development of renewable energy sources to reduce dependence on foreign oil, alongside other energy sources.
positions.quote: I will continue to strongly support the development of renewable energy sources that reduce our dependence on foreign oil and create new, innovative green jobs for Hoosiers.

positions.summary: States on his official site that he opposes efforts to cut Medicaid and will keep working to protect and expand coverage.
positions.quote: I strongly oppose efforts to cut Medicaid and will continue fighting to protect and expand coverage for those who need it most.

record.text: Serves on the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence for the 2025-2026 Congress.
Chaired the Intelligence Committee's Counterterrorism, Counterintelligence, and Counterproliferation Subcommittee during the 2021-2022 Congress.
Served as Ranking Member of the Intelligence Committee's Central Intelligence Agency subcommittee during the 2023-2024 Congress.

candidates.name: Patrick McAuley
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary with 84.4% of the vote.

priorities.text: Says his campaign is focused on homelessness, housing, public safety and jobs.
priorities.quote: We've been focused strictly on local issues: homelessness, housing, public safety, and jobs

priorities.text: Says he would start with helping people build credit.
priorities.quote: what we are looking at doing right away is helping people build credit.

priorities.text: Says he would prioritize trades, apprenticeships and skilled-job opportunities.
priorities.quote: Patrick will prioritize expanded trades, apprenticeships, and skilled-job opportunities so Indianapolis residents can build careers, raise families, and stay in the communities they call home.

statements.quote: Patrick will fight to expand housing supply, convert vacant properties into productive use, and support practical pathways off the street through partnerships and federal resources.
statements.context: On his campaign site, written in the third person

statements.quote: We do have to have a standard for letting people into this country, but we have to do it in a way that stands with the values that this country was built off of
statements.context: In a WFYI interview, asked about how ICE has been used

candidates.researchNotes: Statements are from his campaign issues page and a WFYI interview. He has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey. He said Indiana needs voter IDs; that is not the same as the guide's documentary-proof-of-citizenship issue, so it is not recorded. His site lists public safety goals without addressing police funding, so none is recorded.

candidates.name: James Sceniak
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Libertarian Party of Indiana's March 22, 2026 convention.
candidates.currentRole: Libertarian Party of Indiana Vice Chair

priorities.text: Supports medical freedom, including opposing federal vaccine mandates and supporting descheduling cannabis.
priorities.quote: Vaccinations should not be mandated from the federal level. The federal government should be prohibited from making a sweeping blanket decision.

priorities.text: Proposes a 'VetCare' program that would redirect VA funding into personal care accounts for veterans.
Says his priorities include constitutional security with privacy and lower taxes.
priorities.quote: we want more constitutional security with privacy. We want lower taxes

statements.quote: the tactics we're using with ICE, absolutely unconstitutional. We have to look at, we do have to have borders. We do have to have security, but we have to look at the enforcement.
I don't think big corporations should get tax cuts. I think you know the data centers should be paying their fair share.
statements.context: In a WFYI interview, on data center development

candidates.researchNotes: Statements are from a WFYI interview (July 29, 2026) and the prior campaign site text quoted on Ballotpedia. He has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. His answer on removing U.S. troops from Iran is not recorded under War Powers because it did not address congressional approval.

researchNotes: Patrick McAuley has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; no biography was found, and his statements are from his campaign issues page and a WFYI interview. James Sceniak's cited priorities come from a campaign website republished by Ballotpedia from a prior (Senate) run, not a 2026-specific statement; treat as background rather than a current position. Carson's federal key votes and FEC totals are added separately by script. No campaign website was loaded for Patrick McAuley and he has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; his biography comes from a BallotReady candidate profile and may be incomplete. James Sceniak's biography is drawn from Ballotpedia and a BallotReady profile; he has not completed a 2026 Candidate Connection survey.
